claims.text: USGS recorded a magnitude 5.5 earthquake on 19 July 2026 at 02:24:35 UTC, 4 km SSW of Chupaca, Peru, at a depth of about 10 km, with a PAGER alert level of Yellow ("some casualties and damage are possible and the impact should be relatively localized").

description: USGS recorded a magnitude 5.5 earthquake on 19 July 2026 at 02:24:35 UTC, 4 km SSW of Chupaca in Peru's Andean Junín Region, at a shallow depth of about 10 km. USGS's PAGER system assessed a Yellow alert, indicating some casualties and relatively localized damage were possible. International press reported several deaths, dozens of injuries, and damage to homes and hospital buildings in and around the regional capital Huancayo, but no authoritative source cited by this record has published a confirmed casualty or damage figure, and no GDACS or ReliefWeb disaster report was opened for the event. Three weeks after the mainshock, USGS's event page had not been revised with any new PAGER product and no follow-on activity had been reported; the acute phase has concluded and the event is considered resolved.

impact.summary: USGS assessed a PAGER Yellow alert for the magnitude 5.5 quake near Chupaca (depth about 10 km). No confirmed death, injury, or damage figure has been published by USGS, GDACS, or ReliefWeb; press reports of several deaths, dozens of injuries, and damage around Huancayo remain unconfirmed. USGS's event page has not been revised since the initial PAGER assessment, consistent with the acute phase having concluded.

name: M5.5 Earthquake — Chupaca, Junín Region, Peru
